$comment: What this SDK was built against, and the gate that keeps it honest.
ONE PIN. 'contracts' is the build of arcnow.io's one stack (the multi-quote constant-product
curve under the fee model with no developer share, and the claim-based fee hook with the pool's
own 0.80% rate): its ABIs are abi/*.json and its vectors vectors/vectors.json, pinned to the
arcnow-io/contracts commit that records BOTH deployments, Arc testnet and Arc mainnet, which
networks.json records as contractsCommit.
The maintainers' pin gate enforces, and their preflight runs it:
1. ALWAYS - every file under abi/ and vectors/ hashes to what is recorded here; the ABI set has
the fee-model curve's shape (y0Wad and virtualTokenReserveWad, no kWad, a three-address
previewFeeSplit and no devShareBps anywhere) so a set from another build cannot be recorded
as this one; and the generated copies under rust/src/generated/ and typescript/src/generated/
are byte-identical projections.
2. WHEN A CONTRACTS CHECKOUT IS PRESENT - the same bytes exist at the pinned commit, and
networks.json matches the deployment record in exports/addresses.json at 'addresses.commit',
for every network the record and this file both name. The gate takes the checkout's path;
it can be told to treat a missing one as a failure.
MOVING A PIN is a commit of its own: change the commit, re-copy from exports/, record the hashes,
re-run the sync and the preflight, and say what changed in the ABIs.
ABIs for contracts arcnow.io did not write and does not deploy. The pin is WEAKER
than the one below it and is filed separately so that it cannot be mistaken for it:
an arcnow.io ABI can be re-derived from a commit of arcnow-io/contracts and checked
byte for byte, and one of these cannot be re-derived from anything in this
repository. What is recorded instead is the address it was written against, the
keccak256 of the runtime code there, and how that code was identified. sha256 then
catches an edit to the file after the fact.
IF THE CODEHASH AT THAT ADDRESS EVER CHANGES, the ABI is describing a contract that
no longer exists. arcnow-io/contracts' script/check-deployed-addresses.sh asks the
chain; this file only records the answer.

identified_by: arcnow-io/contracts deploys this contract itself, from creation bytecode that
script/check-router-build.sh proves is exactly what the pinned upstream commit builds
to with upstream's own compiler settings. That build equals Uniswap's mainnet
deployment 0x00000000000044a361Ae3cAc094c9D1b14Eece97 except at seven immutable sites
expected_address is where CREATE2 through Arc's deterministic factory puts it, with
expected_codehash is keccak256 of its runtime with those immutables filled in. address
stays null until the deployment is broadcast, and must equal expected_address.
The five selectors this ABI declares were checked against the upstream build's method
UniswapV4Router04.json.partial: Declares only what this SDK calls. Upstream also exposes multicall(bytes[]), msgSender(), multi-hop swaps over PathKey[], a generic swap(int256,...), swap(bytes,uint256), and a LibZip calldata-decompression fallback.

why: The fee-model (v4) stack as DEPLOYED on Arc testnet AND Arc mainnet: arcnow-io/contracts main at
e461106 (#32, the mainnet deployment record). The build is #27's fee model - no developer share,
FeeShare {Creator, Platform, Ref, Protocol}, the curve's 1.00% split creator 3000 / ref 1000 /
platform 3500 / protocol 2500, and a pool whose hook takes its own 0.80% split creator 5000 /
platform 1875 / protocol 3125 beside a 0.20% LP fee; launching is free (LAUNCH_FEE_WAD = 0).
exports/abi is byte-identical at a514e0a (the commit the testnet manifest records), at 5f1ceb4
(the commit the mainnet manifest records) and at e461106: the ABI did not change after #27.

$comment: WHETHER THE ABIs ABOVE ARE DEPLOYED. 'deployed' means the pinned ABIs are what is on chain:
networks.json records the addresses of this same build, its contractsCommit equals the pin, and
the template gate compares each live platform's template against curve-templates.json. The
fee-model stack was broadcast on Arc testnet at block 62,386,232 and on Arc mainnet at block
21,179,866; the retired multi-quote (v3) testnet stack of 327f45b, at 62,226,550, is gone from
arcnow.io and its data was wiped.
networks.json against arcnow-io/contracts exports/addresses.json, the deployment record, for
EVERY network listed under 'networks' here: Arc testnet (5042002) and Arc mainnet (5042). The pin
gate compares every address (case-insensitively), every contractVersions entry and the deployment
block, and fails if either file carries a legacyStacks key: there is one stack per chain. The
SDKs' arcnowPlatform is the record's platform, and the SDKs' deployedAtBlock the record's
deploymentBlock; both are public API in both SDKs. quoteRegistry is compared the same way.

chain.$comment: Where the tests fork from, and at which block. Addresses live in networks.json, not here. The block is PINNED so a fork suite asserts against the same chain state on every run: 62390000 is after the fee-model stack's deployment on Arc testnet (62,386,232), after arcnow.io's platform was set to the testnet template for both quotes and after EURC was registered, so the addresses networks.json records carry code in the fork and the suites read the live stack as well as deploying their own. It was 62226900 while the multi-quote (v3) stack was live, and 61926859 while the version-2 stack was. Override with ARCNOW_SDK_FORK_BLOCK=<n> (or 'latest') to fork elsewhere; the public endpoint serves historical state.

images.$comment: Pinned, never 'latest'. The same Foundry image arcnow-io/e2e-tests pins, so a fork that behaves differently there behaves differently here for a reason somebody chose.

toolchains.$comment: Exact, never a range and never auto-detected. Every other repository in this project pins the same Rust release; a toolchain that moves under a suite turns 'the system broke' and 'the compiler moved' into the same red run.
